Invite others, clarify rules and swap roles or opponents if helpful. At about 9:25, give a ten-minute warning and return equipment so French starts at 9:35. Optional quiet music; keep instructions audible.

blocks.title: Finish work & prepare for Open House
blocks.notes: Start with each student selecting one incomplete piece worth finishing or improving. Show where completed work goes and which decorating jobs are available. Small groups handle safe decorating tasks; adults handle high displays. Check names on work, choose one piece students would like to explain to family, and make clear display labels. Early finishers use colouring books. Optional low-volume music; pause for instructions. Use the music resources link for instrumental options, not as an automatic playlist. If replacing this block with Orange Shirt Day reading, use the intended reviewed text and give it time for questions and reflection.
studentSteps: Choose one unfinished piece and decide what it needs next.
Finish or improve it, then place it where your teacher shows you.
Help with an available decorating job. Keep walkways clear.
Choose one thing you would like to explain to your family at Open House.
Finished? Enjoy a colouring book, drawing or quiet reading.

blocks.notes: Lunch and the usual school supervision routine.

blocks.notes: Quiet reset. Students choose reading, drawing or colouring. Keep sound low or off if needed for concentration. Have materials ready so this stays a calm transition.

blocks.title: Five Agreements · practise together
blocks.notes: Open the new step-by-step resource. Suggested flow: 1:00–1:08 physical cards and five classroom ideas; 1:08–1:13 teacher model; 1:13–1:25 pairs rehearse or draw; 1:25–1:35 share selected examples; 1:35–1:40 choose one action. blocks.title: Planners & forms to take home
blocks.notes: Distribute planners and device-use forms before packing up. Students write the reminder below and put the form inside the planner. Explain where signed forms will be returned; use an existing collection spot or clearly designate one now. Do not invent a due date. Check quietly that everyone received both. Provide an accessible copy or help writing. Confirm the fee item is live before asking families to pay; any questions about cost can be discussed privately.
studentSteps: Write your name in your planner and put the device-use form inside.
Planner reminder: “Please read and sign the device-use form and return it to school.”
Planner reminder: “Please pay $6 for the planner through School Cash Online.”
Show the reminder and form to your grown-up. Pack both in your bag.

blocks.title: Early cleanup & pack up
blocks.notes: Begin early enough to protect outdoor play. Everyone restores their work area; captains help with shared supplies and bins. Check the display, floors and game pieces. Pack planners/forms and prepare for the regular dismissal routine before leaving.

blocks.title: Capture the Flag
blocks.notes: Use the simple no-elimination version from Day 2, keeping the same rules if already learned. Cones mark territories and a no-camping flag zone. Gentle arm/shoulder tags only in the other team’s territory; tagged players return home, setting down any flag for defenders to reset. Bring the other flag across the centre line to score; reset after a point. Demonstrate the stop signal, include varied movement roles, and use short rounds. Confirm return time before starting; leave time to collect equipment and dismiss calmly. If outdoor space/weather does not work, run an indoor cooperative movement circuit.
studentSteps: Review the boundaries, flag zones and stop signal.
Bring the other flag across the centre line to score for your team.
Tag gently on an arm or shoulder. No pushing, grabbing or tackling.
If tagged in the other territory, return home before trying again. Put down any flag for the other team to reset.
Defenders stay outside the marked flag zone. Freeze at the stop signal.
Help collect equipment and return together when called.

Optional maths replacement: write 6,307 in expanded form; explain the zero. Compare 0.5 and 0.05 and explain with a drawing. Teacher answers: 6,000 + 300 + 7; zero tens; 0.5 is greater because five tenths is greater than five hundredths.

If everyone finishes quickly: chess, a partner puzzle, another conversation card, drawing or existing colouring books. Extra Werewolf can wait; next time review keeping hidden information private, including looks and comments after leaving the game.
